claims_about_writeup.why: The write-up's Controls section does contain all the listed items: random-vector control (neutral, log-rank 2.345), reversed control (3.03), dropping a third of pairs (16 items, cosine 0.96), later-band steering being worse, the flat dose plateau (norms 4.5-5.0 give 17 passes), and ~25 rejected alternative contrasts all at or below baseline — matching the message's bullet list point for point.

differences.what: The message adds an explicit performance/strength comparison ('gain is modest compared to', 'stronger concept-active mode') to the source that the write-up does not make; the write-up only contrasts the construction/mechanism, not relative strength or magnitude of effect.
differences.message_quote: the gain is modest compared to what the white-bear (think/don't-think) method in `papers/` achieves on this exact setup — that direction is a stronger "concept-active" mode
differences.writeup_quote: It is deliberately *not* the white-bear/think-don't-think stance direction (Raman et al., `papers/raman2026-white-bear-steering.md`), which contrasts an instruction about a *named* concept on an otherwise fixed carrier sentence; here there is no named concept, no instruction, and no suppression side

differences.what: The message explicitly frames avoiding the source as a task instruction ('asked not to reproduce'), a framing/explanation absent from the write-up, which instead frames the distinction purely in terms of mechanistic/construction novelty.
differences.message_quote: it's the existing method I was asked not to reproduce
differences.writeup_quote: This is a contrastive-activation-addition construction (difference of conditional means, added to the residual stream) applied to a contrast that, to our knowledge, has not been used

message_source_quote: the gain is modest compared to what the white-bear (think/don't-think) method in `papers/` achieves on this exact setup — that direction is a stronger "concept-active" mode, and it's the existing method I was asked not to reproduce
writeup_source_quote: It is deliberately *not* the white-bear/think-don't-think stance direction (Raman et al., `papers/raman2026-white-bear-steering.md`), which contrasts an instruction about a *named* concept on an otherwise fixed carrier sentence; here there is no named concept, no instruction, and no suppression side — the two conditions differ only in whether the shared content is stated literally or figuratively.
rationale: Both documents name the source (Raman 2026's white-bear/think-don't-think steering) and explicitly position the submitted figurative-mode method as distinct from it rather than as a reproduction, so both treat it primarily as a named contrast/baseline rather than a basis the method builds on. The message goes further than the write-up by adding an explicit comparative performance claim ('gain is modest compared to' the source, which is called a 'stronger concept-active mode') and by framing the avoidance of the source as an explicit task instruction ('asked not to reproduce'), neither of which appears in the write-up's purely mechanistic/constructional contrast.
